terms.meaning: A quadrilateral whose angles are all 90°.
A quadrilateral with all angles equal and all sides equal.
A quadrilateral whose two pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
A quadrilateral with all four sides equal.
A quadrilateral with two separate pairs of equal sides, each pair next to each other.
A quadrilateral with at least one pair of parallel opposite sides. If the other two sides are equal, it is an isosceles trapezium.

items.name: Diagonals of a rectangle
items.formula: Equal, and they bisect each other
items.example: If a diagonal is 10 cm, the other is 10 cm too, and each part is 5 cm.

items.name: Sides of a rectangle
items.formula: Opposite sides are equal and parallel
items.example: A rectangle with sides 7 cm and 4 cm has perimeter 2 × (7 + 4) = 22 cm.

items.name: Diagonals of a square
items.formula: Equal, and they bisect each other at 90°
items.example: They also cut each 90° corner into 45° + 45°.

items.name: Angles of a parallelogram
items.formula: Opposite angles are equal. Adjacent angles add up to 180°.
items.example: If one angle is 70°, the angles are 70°, 110°, 70° and 110°.

items.name: Sides of a parallelogram
items.example: Sides of 9 cm and 5 cm give perimeter 2 × (9 + 5) = 28 cm.

items.name: Diagonals of a parallelogram
items.example: A diagonal of 12 cm is cut into two parts of 6 cm.

items.name: Diagonals of a rhombus
items.formula: They bisect each other at 90°, and bisect its angles
items.example: Diagonals of 6 cm and 8 cm: each side is 5 cm, because 3² + 4² = 5².

items.name: Diagonals of a kite
items.formula: They cross at 90°, and one bisects the other
items.example: If the bisected diagonal is 8 cm, it is cut into 4 cm + 4 cm.

items.name: Angles on a side of a trapezium
items.formula: Angles between the parallel sides add up to 180°
items.example: If one of them is 65°, the other is 180° − 65° = 115°.

items.name: Isosceles trapezium
items.formula: The angles opposite the equal sides are equal
items.example: If one base angle is 75°, the other base angle is 75°.

items.name: Family of quadrilaterals
items.example: Every square is a rectangle, but not every rectangle is a square.

items.name: Where the rhombus fits
items.example: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus. A rhombus is also a kite.

mistakes.text: The diagonals of a parallelogram need not be equal. They are equal only in a rectangle.
The diagonals of a rhombus need not be equal. They cross at 90°, but are equal only in a square.
A trapezium has at least one pair of parallel sides, so a parallelogram also counts as a trapezium.
In a kite the equal sides are next to each other. In a parallelogram they are opposite each other.
The angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°, not 180°. Two triangles make one quadrilateral: 180° + 180° = 360°.
